title: Decision Support Board: Incident Triage and Escalation Runbook
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview

This runbook describes the Decision Support Board (DSB) pattern we use to make high‑velocity, low‑regret decisions during platform incidents that threaten customer-facing SLOs or billing integrity. The DSB is a bounded, cross-functional ad hoc team that supplements the oncall responder pair when an incident requires strategic tradeoffs (for example: service-wide graceful degradation, targeted tenant eviction, or a fast model switchover). This document includes activation criteria, roles and responsibilities, a stepwise decision procedure, alert-to-decision timelines, operator tooling, and after‑action requirements.

Scope

- Applies to platform incidents impacting: hosted inference API, Dedicated routing plane, KV prefix cache, batching router, or cost-exposure pipelines.
- Not intended for routine operator tasks that can be resolved by standard runbooks (see service-specific runbooks).
- Intended for incidents with either: sustained SLO burn >2x normal within 30m, or risk of >$50k/hour customer billing leakage, or multi-region availability degradation.

Why a Decision Support Board?

- Rapid, aligned decisions reduce firefighting churn and unnecessary rollbacks.
- DSB creates a single authority for tradeoffs spanning performance, cost, and customer impact.
- Keeps operators focused on stabilization while product/finance/security weigh long‑term implications.

DSB Composition and Roles

Minimum DSB (15–45 minute focused meeting):
1. Incident Lead (IL) — typically the primary oncall engineer; facilitates and owns the timeline.
2. Platform Tech Lead (PTL) — senior engineer with deep knowledge of the runtime and batcher.
3. Product Liaison (PL) — product manager for affected surface (API/Dedicated/Private).
4. Customer Success Rep (CS) — if customers are actively impacted or billing exposure exists.
5. Ops/Capacity Representative (OR) — SRE responsible for global capacity decisions (evictions, scaling).
6. Finance Representative (FR) — for cost exposure >$20k/hour or contractual concerns.
7. Security Representative (SR) — if the incident includes data access, keys, or compliance risk.

Optional: Legal, Sales ENG, or Partner Manager if the incident touches enterprise contracts or partner regions.

Activation Criteria (automated and manual)

Automated triggers (one of):
- p99 request latency for inference API > 3x SLO for > 30 minutes across >=2 regions.
- Aggregate token generation rate anomaly indicating 4x expected token burn and billing pipeline lag > 10 minutes.
- KV prefix cache eviction rate > 2x baseline leading to >10% cold-start error rate.

Manual triggers (any):
- Oncall believes the incident will require strategic tradeoffs (eviction, scheduled model swap, temporary higher latency SLO).
- Customer escalation to oncall with potential contractual SLA breach.

Decision Timeline and Timeboxes

1. Detection: 0–5m — Alerts fire; oncall ack and initial mitigation begins.
2. Convene DSB: 5–20m — If activation criteria met, Incident Lead pages DSB; meeting started within 20m of trigger.
3. Rapid Assessment: 20–35m — PTL presents impact slice (latency/throughput, affected regions, top tenants by RPS and token burn).
4. Options generation: 35–50m — DSB lists up to 5 options with quick impact/cost estimates.
5. Decision: 50–60m — DSB selects an option and assigns owners and success/fail criteria.
6. Execute & Monitor: 60–180m — Operators implement changes, DSB tracks chosen metrics at 5–15 minute cadence.
7. Reassess / Escalate: every 60m — If metrics not improving by agreed threshold, DSB either escalates to exec oncall or reverts and tries alternate.

Decision Options Catalog (non-exhaustive)

- Controlled degradation: increase per-tenant rate limits, enable lower-quality quantized model variants for selected tenants.
- Targeted tenant evacuation: temporarily move heavy tenants to dedicated burst pool or restrict their throughput.
- Model swap: swap the serving model to a lower-latency/less-costly variant (requires validated fallback & warmup).
- Global throttling: introduce soft queueing with token budget enforcement for free-tier users.
- Capacity expansion: request immediate autoscale/burst from Dedicated pool (if available).
- Billing circuit breaker: pause billing ingestion for suspected runaway token events (Finance signoff).

Decision Matrix (example)

| Symptom | Immediate operator action | DSB preferred option | Success metric (30m) | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| p99 latency spike across regions | Restart batcher & probe kernel metrics | Controlled degradation (enable q4x variant for >10% traffic) | p99 latency back to <1.5x SLO | PTL + Ops |
| Continuous token surge from 2 tenants | Rate-limit offending tenants | Targeted tenant evacuation to burst pool | Token burn reduced by >=60% | OR + CS |
| Billing pipeline lag causing double-count risk | Pause billing ingestion and snapshot offsets | Billing circuit breaker + manual ledger reconciliation | No additional billing records ingested for next 60m | FR |
Note: the table above is presented in monospaced ASCII for Confluence. Replace with the official table macro when publishing.

Operational Playbook: Step-by-step

1. Incident Lead: acknowledge and create/annotate incident ticket (use template: incident/PROD-<YYYYMMDD>-<INCID>).
2. Oncall pair runs stabilization checklist (see Appendix A) and captures: top-10 tenants by token rate, top-10 traces for p95/p99, current capacity and eviction headroom.
3. Page DSB with short TL;DR and required attendees. Use the dedicated Slack channel #dsb-incident.<INCID>. Use the DSB page template link appended to ticket.
4. PTL presents a one-slide impact snapshot (prepared from telemetry queries):
   - SLO burn (1h/6h/24h), top regions, top tenants, cache miss rate, batcher queue depth.
5. DSB runs through Options Catalog; each option gets a 3-line impact statement and 2–3 minute feasibility check.
6. Vote and select option: IL records decision in ticket with expected metric targets and rollback criteria.
7. Operators implement and monitor at 5–15 minute cadence; PL communicates to affected squads and CS performs customer comms as needed.

Rollback & Safety Criteria

- Every DSB decision must include explicit rollback triggers (metric thresholds or elapsed time). Example: "If p99 latency not reduced to <2x SLO within 45 minutes of controlled degradation, immediately revert to previous config and escalate."
- Any change that touches billing ingestion or ledgers requires FR approval and an explicit reconciliation plan before unpausing.

Operator Tooling and Commands

- Telemetry quick queries (templated saved queries):
  - Top tenants by token burn: rql:metrics.top_tokens_by_tenant(last_30m, limit=20)
  - Batcher queue depth: rql:service.queue_depth(service=batcher, last_10m)
  - KV eviction rate: rql:cache.evictions(prefix_kv, last_60m)

- Safe feature flip (example):
  - curl -X POST https://platform-api.internal/api/v1/feature-flips \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
      -d '{"feature":"q4x-serving","tenants":["tenant-a","tenant-b"],"enable":true,"reason":"DSB:controlled-degradation"}'

- Targeted tenant rate limit (CLI helper):
  - platformctl tenant apply-quota --tenant-id <TENANT> --rps 0.5 --duration 60m --reason "DSB mitigation"

Alert and Communication Templates

- Slack alert header (post to #dsb-incident.<INCID>):
  - :rotating_light: DSB ACTIVATION: <INCID> — p99 latency 3.8x SLO in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Paging DSB: IL @oncall, PTL @ptl, OR @ops, PL @product. TL;DR: potential global degradation and token burn spike.

- Customer-facing comms (CS template):
  - Subject: Incident affecting Redwood inference performance in <region>
  - Body: "We are currently investigating elevated latency for inference requests in <region>. Engineers have activated a targeted mitigation plan to restore service and reduce customer impact. We will provide an update in 30 minutes or earlier. If you see functional impact, contact support@redwood.com with your request id."

Post‑Incident Requirements

- Within 24 hours: IL and PTL produce an incident timeline and decision log (decision reasons, options considered, who voted). Attach to the incident ticket.
- Within 72 hours: DSB sponsors (PTL + PL) lead a 60m blameless review focused on decision quality: were tradeoffs correctly weighed, were rollback triggers appropriate, and were communications timely?
- Owner(s) of chosen option open follow-up work (implementation to avoid repeat): e.g., automatic tenant throttles, improved model variant warmup, billing circuit breakers, new SLI query.

KPIs for DSB effectiveness

- Mean time to decision (target: <= 60 minutes).
- Fraction of DSB decisions that required rollback (target: < 25%).
- Post-incident customer escalations attributable to DSB decisions (target: 0).
- Time from DSB activation to stable SLOs (target: < 3 hours for major incidents).

Appendix A — Stabilization Checklist for Operators

1. Collect incident context: affected services, regions, top traces, offending tenant list.
2. Snapshot capacity: GPU pool headroom, batcher queue size, warm model instances.
3. Validate telemetry: ensure sampling not masking burst (check full ingest stream).
4. Apply short-term mitigations with safe defaults: small per-tenant rate limits, bump routing SLO tolerance, or enable a previously-validated quantized variant.
5. Avoid broad schema or data migrations during active incident.

Appendix B — Example Decision Log Entry (template)

- decision_id: DSB-<INCID>-1
- time: 2026-01-12T15:02:00Z
- decision_maker_set: [Priya Desai (IL), Marco Alvarez (PTL), Sofia Nguyen (PL)]
- option_selected: Controlled degradation (enable q4x variant for highest-traffic tenants)
- rationale: Reduce p99 latency quickly while limiting capacity expansion cost; q4x validated on canary.
- expected_success: p99 latency < 1.5x SLO within 45m; token burn reduced by 30% for impacted tenants.
- rollback_criteria: If p99 latency not below 2x SLO in 45m, disable q4x and escalate to exec oncall.
- owners: PTL (execute), OR (monitor capacity), CS (customer comms)

Publishing and Maintenance

- This runbook is reviewed quarterly by Eng Platform leadership.
- Any changes to activation thresholds must be approved by SRE and Finance reps.

Related artifacts

- Saved telemetry queries (link to query library), DSB Slack templates, incident ticket template, and feature-flip API reference.
